item.text: {"text":"Closest evidence: [HSTU-BLaIR (2025)](https://kdd2025llm4ecommerce.github.io/assets/accepted/13_HSTU_BLaIR_Lightweight_Cont.pdf) preserves HSTU and adds projected text embeddings to trainable item IDs. Reported relative HR@10 gains over HSTU range from 2.9% to 22.5% across three Amazon subsets, plus 6% on Steam. However, its encoder uses pretrained Amazon reviews/metadata, making the implementation unsuitable for this task’s restrictions; results do not establish benefits from tokens trained from scratch. [Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) identifies differing ID/text characteristics as a weakness of direct addition, supporting careful fusion rather than assuming lexical similarity improves recommendations.\n\nPractical first experiment—an engineering hypothesis, not a verified recipe from these papers: retain the corrected HSTU backbone and objective; jointly train compact token embeddings and separate title/description pooling, with a small projection into the item-ID space. Preserve identifying numbers, units, model names and short phrases that distinguish compatibility or function. Normalize the text branch before applying a learned residual scale initialized small; mask missing fields explicitly so absent text contributes exactly zero. Apply the same item representation consistently to histories and candidate scoring within one network. Interaction supervision can learn purchase-relevant distinctions, but experiential qualities absent from titles/descriptions remain unobserved. Judge this hypothesis only through the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10; published results use different datasets and protocols."}
